title: Data Science: from stochastics to machine learning with Python
description:
An undergraduate introduction to data science that begins with stochastics and ends with machine learning without leaving a gap in between. The estimators and learning algorithms — k-means, principal component analysis, regression, expectation maximization — are reimplemented rather than called.

Thirty chapters covering probability spaces, random variables and distributions; expected value, variance and the central limit theorem; vectorised computation with Numpy and Scipy; exploratory data analysis with Pandas and Matplotlib; multivariate statistics, covariance and relative entropy; statistical models, maximum likelihood, tests and model selection; and data protection under the GDPR.

The English edition of the lecture notes used in the computer science bachelor's programme at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf. Published as a website and as a 318-page PDF; sources, including every notebook, at github.com/konradvoelkel/ds-en.
notes: Translated from the German original (ds-skript) and kept in step with it chapter by chapter; the mapping and the staleness tooling are in sync/ in the source repository.
